THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 07.03.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 MACA. No.480/2016  3  2025:KER:20374  JUDGMENT Dated this the 7th day of March, 2025
The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.4/2014 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ottapalam is the appellant herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 25.10.20013.

According to the petitioner, on 25.10.2013 at about 6 p.m., while he was riding a motor cycle,
another motor cycle bearing registration No.KL 52A 1453 ridden by the 1 st respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit against his motor cycle and as a result of which he fell down and sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the rider, the 2 nd respondent is the owner and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the 2025:KER:20374 offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.35,00,000/-.
4.
The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Anto vs Muhammed Basheer on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124263859/
2 5.
The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimonies of PW1 and PW2 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A16 series.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.18,06,900/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
9. Heard Sri. Sheji P. Abraham, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri.P. Jacob Mathew, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid insurance policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.

According to him, the petitioner was a tile worker,
earning Rs. 15,000/- per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs7,000/-.
The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the Tribunal is reasonable.
11. It is true that the petitioner could not prove his income, as claimed in the OP.
According tothe petitioner fom his profession as a tile worker, he used to earn Rs.15,000/- permonth.

PW1-his wife,
deposed before the court that her husband was a tile worker getting a daily income of Rs.800/-.

As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2013 will come to Rs.9,000/-.

Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the petitioner being tile worker by profession, his notional income is fixed at Rs.10,000/-, for the purpose of computing the loss of disability.

12. In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
"Abrasion over face, abrasion over right hand, 2025:KER:20374 intracranial bleed,
severe head injury with right posterior temporal contusion with IVH with fracture right temporal bone with diffuse SAH, post traumatic hydrocephalus, small contusion in right temporal lobe, intra cerebral haemorrhage contusion in left parietal lobs."
13.
He was treated as inpatient for a total period of 101 days.
Thereafter he was treated as out patient on various dates.

As per Exhibit A8 disability certificate issued by PW2, the petitioner suffered Anto vs Muhammed Basheer on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124263859/
3 43.75% permanent physical disability.
It was issued by Addl. Professor of Neurosurgeon, attached to Government MCH, Thrissur, who was examined as PW2.

The wife of the petitioner was examined as PW1 and she deposed that the petitioner could not even walk without the help of a bystander and in the above circumstances, the Tribunal fixed his functional disability at 60%.
The petitioner was a tile worker by profession and he was aged 31 years at the time of the accident.
From the evidence of PW1 and from Exhibit A8 disability certificate, it is revealed that the petitioner could not even walk without the help of a bystander.

As such, being a tile worker, he will not be able to do any work or earn anything and as such his functional disability is to be taken as100% on condition that he will not be eligible for compensation on 2025:KER:20374 the head 'loss of earnings'.
14. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 31 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v.
Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 16, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

sentences.text:
In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.26,88,000/-.
15.
Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.35,000/- being the income for 5 months @Rs7,000/-.
Since the functional disability of the petitioner is taken as 100%, he is not eligible for getting any further compensation on the head loss of earnings.

Therefore, Rs.35,000/-
awarded on the head 'loss of earning' will be deducted.
16. The learned counsel would argue that the compensation awarded on the head 'pain and suffering' Rs.40,000/-and extra nourishment Rs.12,600/- are on the lower side.
Further, he would argue that the Tribunal has not awarded any compensation on the head 'loss of amenities'.

Considering the nature injuries sustained by the petitioner, the period during which he was treated as in-patient and otherwise and the percentage of disability suffered by 2025:KER:20374 him, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings', and 'extra nourishment' are on the lower side.
Similarly the Tribunal was also not justified in not awarding compensation on the head 'loss of amenities of life'.

Considering the fact that the petitioner needs the assistance of a bystander for all his needs, I hold that a compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- each on the head 'pain and suffering' and 'loss of amenities' will be a reasonable one.
Similarly, towards the head 'extra nourishment', a sum of Rs.50,000/- will be a reasonable compensation.
17. Towards future medical expenses, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.50,000/-.

Considering the fact that on the date of the accident, the petitioner was only 31 years, he will have to spent a considerable amount towards future treatment including physiotherapy and as such compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the head 'future treatment is on the lower side and hence it is enhanced to Rs.2,00,000/-.
18. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.8,56,800/- for loss of disability and Rs.5,00,000/- for 'continuing partial or permanent disability'.

Since the loss of disability will come to Rs.26,88,000/-,
compensation awarded on the head 'continuing partial or permanent disability' will be adjusted towards the head 'compensation for disability' 2025:

4
19. Rs.12,600/- awarded on the head 'bystander expense' is on the lower side and hence, the amount awarded on the head 'bystander expense is enhanced to Rs.9,60,000/-.
20. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
21. Therefore, the petitioner/appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.5197900/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:

 7 Damage to clothing etc. 500/- 500/-
 8 Pain and suffering 40,000/- 5,00,000/-

9 Compensation for disability 8,56,800/- 26,88,000/
 10 Loss of amenities of life Nil 5,00,000/-
 11 Compensation for continuing partial or 5,00,000/- Nil  permanent disability  Total 18,06,900/- 5197900  Enhanced /Reduced Rs.2443600/-
22.

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and Respondent No.3 is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.51,97,900/- (Rupees fifty one lakhs 2025:KER:20374 ninety seven thousand nine hundred only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest at the rate ordered by the Tribunal, from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation, excluding interest for a period of 200 days, the period of delay in filing the appeal, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.

(Enhanced compensation will carry interest @8%).
23.
On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse 25% of the entire amount, excluding court fee payable, if any, to the petitioner, forthwith.

24. The Tribunal is permitted to decide, after considering the welfare, well being and the best interest of the petitioner, whether the balance amount is to be disbursed in full, forthwith or in installments or to be deposited in a Nationalised bank in fixed deposit in the name of the petitioner and to permit withdrawal of interest alone for the time being.
